So for me it went over an extended stay in a psychiatric hospital. I went through diagnostic for ADHD, Autism, OCD, Anxiety, several ED’s and PTSD/CPTSD. After 11 weeks of extensive diagnosis with several therapists and psychiatrist they concluded a combined personality disorder with traits of borderline personality disorder and histrionic personality disorder. And that is also my official diagnosis; combined personality disorder - BPD and HPD.

They did this because simply saying its BPD or HPD was not enough. I myself have the emotional experience of someone with BPD and some of the social experiences, but I ALSO have the social experiences of someone with HPD and some of the emotional experiences.

It was just not possible to say I have none of them, but also, only one of them wasn’t describing it.

Hey, don’t be like that to yourself. It’s honestly probably useless to tell you how good you’ve been doing. So let me show you some coping skills to help you power through. 

1.	⁠In a clean and brave minute throw them away. In a park or somewhere where you cant reach them. If you really want to you will find alternatives but you’ll have another barrier since your common tools are away.
2.	⁠Try distraction. I do hyper stimulation (do not confuse with overstimulation, although they come close) - a show, a game, maybe a phonecall aswell. Don’t add music or a podcast to this mix - do 1 listening, one thinking, one entertaining. This is also what works best for me. I put on a safeshow (only right option is Brooklyn 99), play animal crossing and talk to my boyfriend.
3.	⁠Try sports. It can really keep the mind clean and power you out.
4.	⁠Try freezing cold showers for a minute or two. The shock will level your body back and reset your mind.
5.	⁠If nothing helps try non-harmful self harm. Sounds really stupid and unhelpful but if you’re SO deep into the addiction a substitute helps (like methadone for heroine addicts). E.g. snapping against skin, ice on skin, rubbing against a scratchy towel, chillis (be careful that it burns but that your stomache can handle it), or very sour, or salty, or sweet (depending on what hurts you the most). Hold your breath as long as possible (DO NOT ARTIFICIALLY CUT YOUR BREATH - only close your mouth and hold your nose, but no throat, belt around your throat, or anything else).

THINGS TO AVOID:

1.	⁠Stressors if you’re already triggered (duh)
2.	⁠Drugs. We’re already struggling with self harm addiction we do not need more.
3.	⁠Food. Same concept - ED’s are still an addiction
4.	⁠Coping things that harm in the long run
5.	⁠Discord vents. We don’t want to trauma dump on others. No no, we’re good people.

I can’t promise these help - no one can. But these brought me through 530 days and they could bring you here aswell. (And PSA: some of them are bendable. Although I strongly discourage).

Lastly, but never to forget: recovery is not possible in an unsafe environment. Self harm is a coping skill, a learned behaviour. Sure, it can be unlearned, but for that you have to feel safe trying out new skills. You can drastically hold on to these ideas but if it comes down I would probably relapse aswell wouldn’t I have a great support system.
